# xmr0.uk — Monero privacy, explained: the protocol, the network and the wallet

> Independent guides to Monero privacy for readers who know security: how ring signatures, one-time addresses and RingCT hide who paid, who was paid and how much; how Dandelion++, Tor and I2P keep a node's address out of a transaction; what view keys, proofs and seeds disclose; and where each protection ends. Written in British English. Every figure names the code, specification or paper it came from and the date it was checked.

How this site works, in four rules:

- **Every figure names where it came from.** A parameter, a date or a version number is the Monero project's, its code's, a specification's or a paper's, and the guide says which and when it was checked.
- **No price talk, no trading advice.** The guides are about how the privacy works, not about buying or selling.
- **Privacy is a security property.** It is explained like encryption: a mechanism, a threat model and limits, and how a holder can disclose a payment on purpose.
- **Nothing here is paid for.** No project, exchange or company pays to be mentioned, ranked or linked.

## What a reader finds here

- [Guides](https://xmr0.uk/guides/): every Monero privacy guide, newest first.
- [The protocol](https://xmr0.uk/protocol/): ring signatures, one-time addresses, RingCT, FCMP++ and the comparison with Zcash.
- [The network](https://xmr0.uk/network/): Dandelion++, and running monerod over Tor or I2P.
- [The wallet](https://xmr0.uk/wallets/): view keys and payment proofs, seeds and Polyseed, signed downloads and hardware wallets.
- [About](https://xmr0.uk/about/): what the site covers and the rules above, written out at length.
- [Everything in one file](https://xmr0.uk/llms-full.txt): every page as Markdown. Each page is also at its own address with `.md` appended.

Mining is not covered here: Monero's proof of work, RandomX, is the subject of [random.directory](https://random.directory/).

## Where the figures come from

The Monero source code (monero-project/monero) and its documentation, Moneropedia, the FCMP++ stressnet release notes, the Carrot and Polyseed specifications, the Dandelion++ paper, the Zcash Improvement Proposals, EUR-Lex for EU law and the Financial Conduct Authority for the UK. Each guide names its source and the date it was checked.

## Guides

- [How Monero privacy works: sender, receiver and amount](https://xmr0.uk/guides/how-monero-privacy-works/): Monero privacy rests on three mechanisms: ring signatures hide which output paid, one-time addresses hide who was paid, and RingCT hides how much. How each one works, and what a transaction still shows.
- [FCMP++: how full-chain membership proofs replace rings](https://xmr0.uk/guides/fcmp-plus-plus/): FCMP++ replaces Monero's 16-member rings with a proof that the output spent is one of every output on the chain. How the proof works, the Carrot address scheme that comes with it, and what Monero privacy gains.
- [Monero vs Zcash: two privacy models compared](https://xmr0.uk/guides/monero-vs-zcash/): Monero privacy is on for every transaction, with 16-member rings; Zcash hides only shielded transactions, but hides them among every note in their pool. How the two models differ, from proofs and keys to the turnstile.
- [Dandelion++: how Monero hides where a transaction began](https://xmr0.uk/guides/dandelion-plus-plus/): Ring signatures hide the sender on the chain, not the node that first broadcast the transaction. How Dandelion++ protects Monero privacy on the network: the stem, the fluff, the embargo and the parameters Monero uses.
- [Running a Monero node over Tor or I2P](https://xmr0.uk/guides/monero-node-over-tor-i2p/): Monero privacy on the chain does not cover the IP address that sent a transaction. How to run monerod over Tor or I2P — --proxy, --tx-proxy, a hidden service for the wallet — and the leaks the project's own documentation lists.
- [What a Monero view key reveals](https://xmr0.uk/guides/monero-view-key/): A Monero view key shows every payment a wallet receives, but not reliably what it spends. What the private view key reveals, what the payment, spend and reserve proofs disclose instead, and how Carrot changes Monero privacy for view-only wallets.
- [Securing a Monero wallet: seeds, signed downloads and hardware](https://xmr0.uk/guides/monero-wallet-security/): Monero privacy is only as good as the wallet holding the keys. How the 25-word seed and Polyseed encode them, how to check a download against the signed hashes, and which hardware wallets the Monero project lists.
- [Privacy coins and the rules in the EU and the UK](https://xmr0.uk/guides/privacy-coins-eu-uk-rules/): What the EU's AMLR and MiCA and the UK's cryptoasset rules say about privacy coins: whom they bind, from which date, and how Monero privacy tools such as view keys and payment proofs sit beside them.
